source.title: Zeta morphisms for rank two universal deformations
readSections: The published version, read in full: the open-access (CC BY 4.0) PDF from link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-023-01203-7.pdf (120 pages, pp. 171–290; SHA-256 47682f856244439d8cc3d3e6e0a4e1f804e6a710ec1a2dde8fad76f94aea20e4; fetched 23 September 2026; received 16 June 2021, accepted 19 May 2023, published online 15 June 2023). Read: §1 (Theorem 1.1, Remark 1.2, Conjecture 1.3, Theorem 1.4, the outline, notation), §2 (completed cohomology, Hecke algebras, Theorem 2.1, Theorem 2.2, completed homology, Lemma 2.4, Corollaries 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Lemmas 2.6, 2.9–2.11), §3 (modular curves, Lemma 3.1, Kato's elements and norm relations (9)–(16), Theorem 3.2, the Drinfeld–Manin splitting, Lemma 3.4, Corollary 3.6, Proposition 3.8, Lemmas 3.9, 3.12, 3.13, Corollaries 3.10, 3.11, 3.14, Proposition 3.15, Theorem 3.16, Proposition 3.17), §4 (Lemma 4.1, Corollary 4.2, Theorems 4.3, 4.5, 4.7, Corollary 4.8, Proposition 4.9 and the proof of Theorem 4.3), §5 (Conjectures 5.1, 5.3, 5.8, 5.10, 5.12, 5.13, Theorem 5.2, Corollaries 5.4, 5.6, 5.15, Lemma 5.5, Theorems 5.7, 5.9, 5.11, 5.14 and their proof), Appendix A (Theorem A.1, Remarks A.2, A.6, Lemma A.3, Definition A.4, Corollary A.5), Appendix B (B.1–B.4) and the references. Page numbers are the journal's; every recorded mistake was checked on the page images.
arXiv 2006.13647 has only v1 (24 June 2020) and v2 (2 July 2020), both before submission; v2 was compared on the recorded passages, all of which it shares, so no later version corrects them.

Cited inputs were not read; items resting on them (Kato 2004, Emerton's local–global compatibility manuscript and 2006 papers, Emerton–Helm, Helm, Paškūnas 2013 and 2015, CEGGPS, Calegari–Emerton, Fukaya–Kato, Böckle, Colmez, Kisin, Henniart, Kim–Lee–Ponsinet, Skinner, Pottharst) state them as the paper uses them.

summary: The paper constructs zeta morphisms z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) : (ρ^u)^* → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], (ρ^u)^*(1)) for the universal deformation of an odd absolutely irreducible ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽) (p ≥ 5, End(ρ̄_p) = 𝔽, ρ̄_p not a twist of (1 ∗; 0 ε^{±1})), satisfying the Euler system relations and interpolating Kato's zeta morphisms z(f) at every modular point up to the Euler factors at Σ∖{p} (Theorems 1.1 and 4.3), as Kato's generalised Iwasawa main conjecture predicts. Method: Fukaya–Kato-style zeta morphisms on the full-level parabolic cohomology of X(N), made integral after localising at ρ̄ and passed to the limit on Emerton's completed Borel–Moore homology, whose dual local–global compatibility reads (P̃ ⊗̂ (ρ^m)^*) ⊗ π̃^m_{Σ_0}; Paškūnas' projective envelope P̃ and Emerton–Helm's Whittaker functor remove the local factors, and Paškūnas' description of Kisin's potentially semistable rings through P̃ identifies the specialisations. Application (§5): congruences of Kato's zeta morphisms and the propagation of μ = 0 and Kato's main conjecture across a residual family. The atlas already plans the construction in AutomorphicCongruences L3, which names Nakamura's morphism, and its suppliers (KatoEulerSystems, CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility, CompletedCohomologyPartII, PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups), so every route is a source of existing layers except Henniart's types, coalesced into SmoothRepresentationsPartII. Fifteen misprints are recorded.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: zeta morphisms for the universal deformation of ρ̄
items.statement: Let p be prime, Σ ∋ p finite, and ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽) odd, absolutely irreducible, unramified outside Σ, with universal deformation ρ^u : G_ℚ → GL_2(R_{ρ̄,Σ}). Assume (1) p ≥ 5; (2) ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible; (3) End_{𝔽[G_{ℚ_p}]}(ρ̄_p) = 𝔽; (4) ρ̄_p is not (1 ∗; 0 ε^{±1}) ⊗ χ. Then there are R_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear maps z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) : (ρ^u)^* → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], (ρ^u)^*(1)) for all n ≥ 1 prime to Σ, with (i) z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u)(τv) = σ_{−1}z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u)(v) (τ complex conjugation); (ii) Cor ∘ z_{Σ,nl}(ρ^u) = z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) if l | n and P_l(σ_l^{−1})·z_{Σ,n}(ρ^u) if (l, n) = 1, where P_l(u) = det(1 − Frob_l·u | ρ^u); (iii) at every point x_f of a normalized Hecke eigen cusp newform f, z_{Σ,1}(f) = ∏_{l∈Σ∖{p}} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{−1})·z(f), with P_{f,l}(u) = det(1 − Frob_l·u | ρ_f^{I_l}) and z(f) Kato's zeta morphism.
items.note: AutomorphicCongruences L3 plans exactly this: 'Construct Nakamura's universal zeta morphism from the compatible modular/Hecke-level classes, including the completed-cohomology and local co-Whittaker input … Prove that this morphism specializes to R12's Kato class.' It combines Corollary 4.2 and Theorem 4.3 (for T_{ρ̄,Σ}) with Böckle's R = T (Theorem 2.1).

items.name: Theorem 4.3: the universal zeta morphism specialises to Kato's
items.statement: Under the assumptions of §4, for every modular point x_f ∈ Spec(T_{ρ̄,Σ})(E) and n ≥ 1 prime to Σ, z_{Σ,n}(f) = ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{−1})·z_n(f) as maps V′_1(f)_E → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], V′_1(f)_E(1)) under V′_1(f)_E ≅ ρ_f^* (57), where Σ_0 = Σ ∖ {p}; the statement does not depend on the choice of (57) since End_{E[G_ℚ]}(ρ_f) = E (Remark 4.4).

items.name: Corollary 4.2: τ-equivariance and Euler system relations for z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m)
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 prime to Σ, z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m)(τv) = σ_{−1}z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m)(v) for v ∈ (ρ^m)^*, and for every prime l ∉ Σ, Cor ∘ z_{Σ,nl}(ρ^m) = z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) if l | n and P_l(σ_l^{−1})·z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) if (l, n) = 1.

items.name: §4.1: construction of z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) by factoring out P̃ and applying the Whittaker functor
items.statement: Fix φ_1 : H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (π^m_p)^* ⊗ (ρ^m)^* ⊗ π̃^m_{Σ_0} (Corollary 2.5; printed 'Proposition 2.5', sourceIssues E4). Lemma 4.1: φ_1 induces H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ}(1)) ≅ (π^m_p)^* ⊗̂ H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], (ρ^m)^*(1) ⊗ π̃^m_{Σ_0}) (via a perfect complex and Corollary B.32). Transporting z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄} (independent of φ_1 by Lemma 2.6), Corollary B.28 gives a unique continuous T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_{Σ_0}]-linear φ_2 with id_{(π^m_p)^*} ⊗ φ_2 = z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄} (52)–(53); applying the Whittaker functor Φ_{Σ_0} (written Ψ_{Σ_0} here, sourceIssues E15) and Φ_{Σ_0}(π̃^m_{Σ_0}) ≅ T_{ρ̄,Σ} gives z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) : (ρ^m)^* → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], (ρ^m)^*(1)) (55), independent of the choices.

items.name: Theorem 1.4: Kato's main conjecture propagates along congruences under μ = 0
items.statement: Assume (1), (3), (4) of Theorem 1.1 for ρ̄ = ρ̄_f. If there are g_1, g_2, g_3 congruent to f with (1) some τ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})) with ρ_{g_1}/(τ − 1)ρ_{g_1} free of rank one over O; (2) μ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/N_{g_2}p], ρ^*_{g_2}(1))/Λ_O·Im z(g_2)) = 0; (3) Conjecture 1.3 for g_3; then μ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/N_fp], ρ_f^*(1))/Λ_O·Im z(f)) = 0 and Conjecture 1.3 holds for f.
items.note: The application of §5 (Theorems 5.7–5.14). Routed as a source of AutomorphicCongruences L4 (pointwise consequences of the universal zeta element).

items.name: Completed cohomology of modular curves Ĥ^i(K^p), Ĥ¹_Σ and the ρ̄-part
items.statement: For compact open K_f ⊂ GL_2(𝔸_f), Y(K_f)(ℂ) = GL_2(ℚ)∖ℍ^± × GL_2(𝔸_f)/K_f; H^i(K^p)_A = lim_{K_p} H^i(K_pK^p)_A with smooth G_p-action, Ĥ^i(K^p) its ϖ-adic completion (with G_ℚ × G_p action), Ĥ^i(K_{Σ_0}) = Ĥ^i(K_{Σ_0}K^Σ_0), Ĥ¹_Σ = lim_{K_{Σ_0}} Ĥ¹(K_{Σ_0}) with inductive-limit topology, and Ĥ¹_{ρ̄,Σ} = lim Ĥ¹(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ (a G_ℚ × G_Σ-stable direct summand); the compactly supported variants, with Ĥ¹_c → Ĥ¹ surjective, T_c ≅ T, and Ĥ¹_{c,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ Ĥ¹_{ρ̄,Σ} for ρ̄ absolutely irreducible.

items.name: Big Hecke algebras T(K_{Σ_0}), allowable levels, T_{ρ̄,Σ}, ρ^m and φ_Σ : R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T_{ρ̄,Σ}
items.statement: T(K_Σ) is generated by S_l, T_l (l ∉ Σ) on H¹(K_ΣK^Σ_0); T(K_{Σ_0}) = lim_{K_p} T(K_pK_{Σ_0}) is a finite product of complete local rings. K_{Σ_0} is allowable for ρ̄ if some maximal ideal 𝔪 with residue field 𝔽 has tr ρ̄(Frob_l) ≡ T_l, det ρ̄(Frob_l) ≡ lS_l; T_{ρ̄,Σ} = lim T(K_{Σ_0})_ρ̄ carries ρ^m : G_ℚ → GL_2(T_{ρ̄,Σ}) with tr ρ^m(Frob_l) = T_l, det = lS_l; the universal deformation ring R_{ρ̄,Σ} (unramified outside Σ ∪ {∞}) maps onto T_{ρ̄,Σ} by φ_Σ.
items.note: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.3 (completed Hecke algebra, its Galois representation and the map from the deformation ring); GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2 (universal rings); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.6.

items.name: Theorem 2.1: Böckle's R = T
items.statement: If p ≥ 3, ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(ζ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible and ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is neither χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 1) nor χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε), then φ_Σ : R_{ρ̄,Σ} → T_{ρ̄,Σ} is an isomorphism.
items.note: Böckle [4, Cor. 3.8] and Emerton [15, Thm. 1.2.3]; CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.6 plans Emerton's Theorems 1.2.3–1.2.4 with these hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 2.2: Emerton's local–global compatibility for Ĥ¹_{ρ̄,Σ}
items.statement: Assume ρ̄_p ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε), p ≥ 3 and End(ρ̄_p) = 𝔽; let π^m_p be the deformation of π̄_p (Theorems B.18, B.20) with MF(π^m_p) ≅ ρ^m|_{G_{ℚ_p}} and, for l ∈ Σ_0, π^m_l the coadmissible T_{ρ̄,Σ}-representation whose contragredient is torsion free, co-Whittaker and generically π̃(ρ_l(𝔞)) (Theorem B.11), π̃^m_{Σ_0} the maximal torsion-free quotient of ⊗_l π̃^m_l and π^m_{Σ_0} its contragredient. Then there is a G_ℚ × G_Σ-equivariant T_{ρ̄,Σ}-linear topological isomorphism ρ^m ⊗ π^m_p ⊗̌ π^m_{Σ_0} ≅ Ĥ¹_{ρ̄,Σ}.
items.note: Emerton [15, Conj. 6.1.6, Thm. 6.4.16] (unpublished manuscript); CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.4 plans exactly this source theorem.

items.name: Completed Borel–Moore homology H̃^BM_1(K^p) and H̃^BM_{1,Σ}
items.statement: H̃^BM_1(K^p) = lim_{K_p} H¹(K_pK^p)(1) along corestriction (≅ lim H_1(X(K_pK^p)(ℂ), {cusps}, O) by Poincaré duality, Remark 2.3), a compact O[[GL_2(ℤ_p)]]-module with G_ℚ × G_p action; restriction maps are injective; H̃^BM_{1,Σ} = lim_{K_{Σ_0}} H̃^BM_1(K_{Σ_0}K^Σ_0) with smooth G_{Σ_0}-action; the Hecke action is by T′_l = T_lS_l^{−1}, S′_l = S_l^{−1}, identified with T(K_{Σ_0}).
items.note: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3 (continuous duals and completed homology) and R31.1.

items.name: Lemma 2.4 and §2.3.2: duality between completed homology and completed cohomology with compact support
items.statement: h_{K^p} : H̃^BM_1(K^p) → Hom_O(Ĥ¹_c(K^p), O) is a topological isomorphism (from the Calegari–Emerton sequence 0 → Hom(Ĥ²_c[ϖ^∞], L/O) → H̃^BM_1 → Hom(Ĥ¹_c, O) → 0 [7, Thm. 1.1.3] and Ĥ²_c = 0 [14, Prop. 4.3.6]); with the normalised projectors p_{K_{Σ_0}} these assemble into a Hecke and G_ℚ × G_Σ-equivariant isomorphism H̃^BM_{1,Σ} ≅ (Ĥ¹_{c,Σ})~ (smooth contragredient), and H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (Ĥ¹_{ρ̄,Σ})~.
items.note: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3 (biduality in the compact/discrete category) with CC.7 (compact support). The printed diagram on p. 195 has a misprint in its corner (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Corollary 2.5: dual local–global compatibility for completed homology
items.statement: Under (a), (b), (c) of §2.2 there is a T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_ℚ × G_Σ]-linear topological isomorphism H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (π^m_p)^* ⊗ (ρ^m)^* ⊗ π̃^m_{Σ_0}.
items.note: From Theorem 2.2, Lemma B.16 and the duality. Routed as a source of CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.4.

items.name: Lemma 2.6 and Corollary 2.7: endomorphisms of the completed homology
items.statement: For A ∈ Comp(O), deformations ρ of ρ̄_p and π of π̄_p over A, and a co-Whittaker A[G_{Σ_0}]-module V, End^cont_{A[G_{ℚ_p}×G_Σ]}(π^* ⊗ ρ^* ⊗ V) = A. Hence End^cont_{T[G_ℚ×G_Σ]}(H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ}) = End^cont_{T[G_{ℚ_p}×G_Σ]}(H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ}) = T_{ρ̄,Σ}, so the isomorphism of Corollary 2.5 is unique up to T^×.
items.note: Uses Lemma B.10 and End(π̄_p) = 𝔽 [15, Rem. 3.3.14]. Routed as a source of R31.4.

items.name: Corollary 2.8: completed homology via Paškūnas' projective envelope
items.statement: Assume (a)′ ρ̄_p ≇ χ ⊗ (1 ∗; 0 ε^{±1}), (b)′ p ≥ 5 and (c) End(ρ̄_p) = 𝔽; let R_p be the universal deformation ring of ρ̄_p and P̃ ∈ C(O) the projective envelope of π_{1,p}^∨ (the dual of the socle of π̄_p), with R_p ≅ End_{C(O)}(P̃). Then H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ (P̃ ⊗̂_{R_p} (ρ^m)^*) ⊗_{T} π̃^m_{Σ_0}, T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_ℚ × G_Σ]-linearly.
items.note: From Corollary 2.5 (cited as 'Proposition 2.5', sourceIssues E4) and Proposition B.26. Routed as a source of R31.4.

items.name: Lemmas 2.9–2.11: completed homology with coefficients recovers classical cohomology
items.statement: For a compact O[[GL_2(ℤ_p)]]-module M, M ⊗̂_O H̃^BM_1(K^p) ≅ H̃^BM_1(K^p, 𝒱_M) Hecke-equivariantly (Lemma 2.9). For an algebraic representation W of GL_2/ℚ_p, W ⊗_{O[[K_p]]} H̃^BM_1(K^p) ≅ H¹(K^pK_p, 𝒱_W)(1) (Lemma 2.10, via [13, Thm. 2.2.17, (4.3.7)] and Poincaré duality), and likewise for M = τ ⊗ W with τ a smooth representation of GL_2(ℤ_p) (Lemma 2.11, by Hochschild–Serre).
items.note: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.2 (classical specialisations of completed cohomology) with CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.6 (descent and classical comparison).

items.name: Modular curves Y(N), X(N), the local systems 𝒱_k and spaces of modular forms
items.statement: For N ≥ 3, Y(N) over ℤ[1/N] is the moduli of (E, e_1, e_2) with (ℤ/N)² ≅ E[N]; X(N) its compactification; 𝒱_{k/A} = Sym^{k−2}(R¹f_*A) and its dual; S_k(N)_A, M_k(N)_A (log poles at cusps); the left GL_2(ℤ/N)-action; the finite maps Y(N) → Y(M) ⊗ μ^0_m (Weil pairing).

items.name: Siegel units and Beilinson elements in K_2
items.statement: For (c, 6) = 1, Kato's cθ_E ∈ Γ(E ∖ E[c], O)^× with div = E[c] − c²[0] and norm-compatibility [28, Prop. 1.3]; c g_{α,β} = ι^*_{α,β}(cθ) on Y(N), with σ^*(c g_{α,β}) = c g_{(α,β)σ}; c,d z_N = {c g_{1/N,0}, d g_{0,1/N}} ∈ K_2(Y(N)) and cz_N = c,c z_N; norm relations (9) Norm(cz_M) = cz_N if prime(M) = prime(N) and (10) Norm(cz_{Nl}) = (1 − T^*(l)(1/l 0; 0 1)^* + l(1/l 0; 0 1/l)^*)cz_N; τ_0(cz_N) = cz_N for τ_0 = (1 0; 0 −1) (Lemma 3.9).

items.name: Kato's elements in Galois and Iwasawa cohomology and their norm relations
items.statement: cz^(p)_N ∈ H¹(ℤ[1/Np], H¹(Y(N))(2)) is the image of cz_N under the Chern class and Hochschild–Serre; the elements cz^(p)_{N_0p^∞} ∈ H¹(ℤ[1/Σ], H̃^BM_1(K^p(N_0))(1)); cz^(p)_N(k, −) : Sym^{k−2}(ℤ_p²)^* → H¹(ℤ[1/Σ], H¹(Y(N), 𝒱_k^*)(2)) via Lemma 2.10; cz^(p)_{N,np^m}(k, −) via Y(N) ⊗ μ^0_{np^m} and Shapiro; cz^Iw_{N,n}(k, −) in Iwasawa cohomology; with the corestriction relations (11)–(16), e.g. Cor ∘ cz^Iw_{N,nl}(k, −) = (1 − T′_l ⊗ σ_l^{−1} + lS′_l ⊗ σ_l^{−2})cz^Iw_{N,n}(k, −) for l ∤ n.
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L1–L2 ('Construct the rational universal class before projecting to the form', moment compatibility, p-direction and away-from-p relations).

items.name: Theorem 3.2: Kato's zeta value formula
items.statement: Let N ≥ 3, n ≥ 1 with prime(Np) = Σ and (n, Np) = 1. For v ∈ Sym^{k−2}(ℤ²)^* and m ≥ 0 the image cω_{N,np^m}(k, v) of cz^Iw_{N,n}(k, v) under the twist by ((ζ_{p^m}))^{⊗(1−k)}, projection, loc_p and exp^* lies in M_k(N)_ℚ ⊗ ℚ(ζ_{np^m}), and per(cω_{N,np^m}(k, v)) = (2πi)^{1−k}Z_{Σ,np^m}(k − 1)·cδ_{N,np^m}(k, v) in H¹(Y(N)(ℂ), 𝒱_{k/ℂ}) ⊗_{ℂ[±1]} ℂ[Gal(ℚ(ζ_{np^m})/ℚ)], where Z_{Σ,n}(s) = ∏_{l∉Σ_n} P_l(l^{−s} ⊗ σ_l^{−1})^{−1} and cδ is the smoothed modular symbol.
items.note: Kato [28, Thms. 4.6, 9.5] reformulated; KatoEulerSystems L3 (explicit reciprocity, dual exponential, period normalisation). Uses PadicHodgeRegulators L1 (dual exponential) and the modular-symbol period map.

items.name: Period maps, the operator zeta function and the smoothed modular symbols

items.name: The Drinfeld–Manin splitting
items.statement: There is a unique T_k(N)_ℚ-linear (hence T′_k(N)_ℚ-linear, Gal(ℂ/ℝ)- and, after ⊗ℚ_p, G_ℚ-equivariant) splitting s_N : H¹(Y(N)(ℂ), 𝒱_{k/ℚ}) → H¹(X(N)(ℂ), j_*𝒱_{k/ℚ}) of the inclusion of parabolic cohomology, inducing s_N : M_k(N)_ℚ → S_k(N)_ℚ.

items.name: Lemma 3.4 and Remark 3.5: Iwasawa cohomology of parabolic cohomology
items.statement: (1) H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱_{k/ℤ_p}(i))) is Λ_n-torsion free for all i; (2) exp^* : H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱_{k/ℤ_p}(1))) → lim_m S_k(N) ⊗ ℚ(ζ_{np^m}) ⊗ ℚ_p is injective. Both fail for Y(N).
items.note: Fukaya–Kato [20, Prop. 3.1.3(1), Lem. 3.1.4] for X_1(N) and k = 2, with 'the same argument' for X(N) and all k. Routed as a source of KatoEulerSystems L3.

items.name: Corollary 3.6: characterisation of s_N(cz^Iw_{N,n}(k, v))
items.statement: s_N(cz^Iw_{N,n}(k, v)) is the unique element of H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱^*_{k/ℚ_p}(2))) whose images ω_m under twist, loc_p and exp^* lie in S_k(N)_ℚ ⊗ ℚ(ζ_{np^m}) with per(ω_m) = (2πi)^{1−k}Z_{Σ,np^m}(k − 1)·s_N(cδ_{N,np^m}(k, v)) (22) in the ℂ[±1]-quotient.
items.note: From Theorem 3.2 and Lemma 3.4(2), using injectivity of can ∘ per from (21). Routed as a source of KatoEulerSystems L3.

items.name: Proposition 3.8: the equivariant zeta morphism z^Iw_{N,n}(k, −) on H¹(Y(N))
items.statement: There is a unique ℤ_p[GL_2(ℤ/N)]-linear z^Iw_{N,n}(k, −) : H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_{k/ℤ_p})(1) → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱^*_{k/ℚ_p}(2)))_{Q_{k,n}} (Q_{k,n} the multiplicative set of the (c² − c^{2−j}σ_c)) with (1) (c² − c^{2−j}σ_c)(c² − c^{j−k+2}σ_c)·z^Iw_{N,n}(k, δ_N(k, e_1^{j−1}e_2^{k−1−j})) = s_N(cz^Iw_{N,n}(k, e_1^{j−1}e_2^{k−1−j})) for c ≡ 1 (mod N), (c, 6pn) = 1; (2) the analogue for all c with (c 0; 0 1)^* ⊗ σ_c; (3) z^Iw_{N,n}(k, τv) = σ_{−1}z^Iw_{N,n}(k, v). It is T′_k(N)_{ℤ_p}-linear and ℋ(N)-linear (Corollary 3.10), satisfies the Euler relations with P_l(σ_l^{−1}) (Corollary 3.11) and is compatible with corestriction and restriction in the level (Lemma 3.12).
items.locator: §3.2, Proposition 3.8 and proof, pp. 223–227; Corollaries 3.10–3.11, Lemma 3.12, pp. 228–230

items.name: Proposition 3.15: integrality of the localised zeta morphism
items.statement: After localising at the non-Eisenstein ideal of ρ̄ (where H¹(X(N), j_*𝒱^*)_ρ̄ ≅ H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*)_ρ̄ and s_N is its inverse), the map z^Iw_{N,n,ρ̄}(k, −) : H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_{k/O})_ρ̄(1) → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_{k/O})_ρ̄(2))_{Q_{k,n}} (Corollary 3.14, (37)) has image in the unlocalised H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H¹(Y(N), 𝒱^*_{k/O})_ρ̄(2)).

Proof: freeness over Λ^0 = ℤ_p[[Γ_0]] (as Kato [28, Thm. 12.4(3)]) reduces to p inverted; the decomposition (38)–(39) by local–global compatibility and strong multiplicity one, new vectors, and Kato's integrality [28, Thm. 12.5] via Corollary A.5 (sourceIssues E5–E7 in the proof).

items.name: Theorem 3.16: the G_Σ-equivariant zeta morphism on completed homology
items.statement: The limits z^Iw_{N_0p^∞,n,ρ̄} (44) and z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄} : H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ}(1)) (45) exist; z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄} is continuous and T_{ρ̄,Σ}[G_Σ]-linear, z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄}(τv) = σ_{−1}z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄}(v), and Cor ∘ z^Iw_{Σ,nl,ρ̄} = z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄} (l | n) or P_l(σ_l^{−1})z^Iw_{Σ,n,ρ̄} (l ∤ n).

items.name: Corollary 4.8 and Proposition 4.9: the classical realisations of M^⋄(k, τ) ⊗ (ρ^m)^*
items.statement: For σ^⋄(k, τ) = Sym^{k−2}(E²)^* ⊗ σ^⋄(τ), σ^⋄(k, τ) ⊗_{O[[K_0]]} H̃^BM_1(K^p(N_0))_ρ̄ ≅ H¹(Y(N_0), 𝒱^*_{k/E}(σ^⋄(τ)))_ρ̄(1) and in the limit σ^⋄(k, τ) ⊗ H̃^BM_{1,ρ̄,Σ} ≅ H¹_{Σ_0}(𝒱^*_{k/E}(σ^⋄(τ)))_ρ̄(1), T^⋄_{ρ̄,Σ}(k, τ) = T ⊗_{R_p} R^⋄_p(k, τ)[1/p] acting (Corollary 4.8); and M^⋄(k, τ) ⊗_{R_p} (ρ^m)^* ≅ Φ_{Σ_0}(H¹_{Σ_0}(𝒱^*_{k/E}(σ^⋄(τ)))_ρ̄)(1), T^⋄[G_ℚ]-linearly, intertwining Φ_{Σ_0}(z^Iw_{Σ_0,n,ρ̄}(k, σ^⋄(τ), −)) with id ⊗ z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m) (Proposition 4.9).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.3: motivic structures on Φ_{Σ_0}(H¹_{Σ_0}(𝒱^*(σ^⋄(τ)))[f]) and comparison with Kato
items.statement: For x_f of Galois type τ (⋄ = cr if ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is potentially crystalline, st otherwise), x_f factors through T^⋄(k, τ) (Theorem 4.5), (M^⋄(k, τ) ⊗ T^⋄)_{𝔪_f} is free of rank one (Theorem 4.7), and z_{Σ,n}(f) is the base change of Φ_{Σ_0}(z^Iw_{Σ_0,n,ρ̄}(k, σ^⋄(τ), −)). The spaces V′_3(f)_A, V_3(f^*)_A, S_3(f^*)_A (75)–(76) are two-, two- and one-dimensional (dim Φ_{Σ_0}(π̃_{Σ_0}(f)) = 1 and dim Hom_{K_0}(σ^⋄(τ), π_p(f)) = 1), V′_3(f)_E ≅ ρ_f^* (77), and via new vectors (V′_4) V′_2(f) ≅ V′_3(f) compatibly with Betti lattices, periods and dual exponentials; the characterisation of Corollary A.5 then gives the theorem.

items.name: Theorem 4.5 and Remark 4.6: Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings (rank two, no fixed determinant)
items.statement: For k ≥ 2 and an inertial type τ : I_p → GL_2(E) there are unique quotients R^st_p(k, τ), R^cr_p(k, τ) of R_p, p-torsion free and reduced after inverting p, whose E′-points are the potentially semistable (resp. potentially crystalline) lifts of type τ with Hodge–Tate weights {−(k − 1), 0}; R^cr_p(k, τ)[1/p] and Spec R^st_p(k, τ)[1/p] ∖ Spec R^cr_p(k, τ)[1/p] are regular.
items.note: Kisin [33] (and [8, §6.1] for varying determinant; [33, Thm. 3.3.8], [35, Thm. A.2]); LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3.

items.name: Henniart's types σ^st(τ), σ^cr(τ)
items.statement: For an inertial type τ there is a unique finite-dimensional absolutely irreducible smooth E-representation σ^st(τ) (resp. σ^cr(τ)) of K_0 = GL_2(ℤ_p) such that for every Frobenius-semisimple two-dimensional Weil–Deligne representation W, π(W)|_{K_0} contains σ^st(τ) (resp. σ^cr(τ)) iff W|_{I_p} ≅ τ (resp. and N = 0); moreover dim Hom_{K_0}(σ^⋄(τ), π(W)|_{K_0}) ≤ 1 (58).
items.note: Coalesced into SmoothRepresentationsPartII (types), as PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B routed Henniart's GL_2 types.

items.name: Theorem 4.7: Paškūnas' description of the potentially semistable rings through P̃
items.statement: Assume p ≥ 5, End(ρ̄_p) = 𝔽 and ρ̄_p ≇ (ε ∗; 0 1) ⊗ η. For M^⋄_0(k, τ) = σ^⋄_0(k, τ) ⊗_{O[[K_0]]} P̃ (σ^⋄_0(k, τ) = Sym^{k−2}(O²)^* ⊗ σ^⋄_0(τ)), R_p/Ann_{R_p}(M^⋄_0(k, τ)) = R^⋄_p(k, τ) for ⋄ ∈ {st, cr}; M^cr(k, τ) is locally free of rank one over R^cr_p(k, τ)[1/p], and M^st(k, τ) is locally free of rank one over Spec R^st_p(k, τ)[1/p] ∖ Spec R^cr_p(k, τ)[1/p].
items.note: Paškūnas [45, Cor. 6.5, Prop. 4.14], CEGGPS [8, Props. 6.12, 6.14], Gee–Newton [21, Rem. 5.1.7]; PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.5 (support and multiplicity in the local Breuil–Mézard results) and R30.6 (Paškūnas 2015, p ≥ 5, scalar endomorphisms).

items.name: Conjecture 1.3 / 5.1: Kato's main conjecture, and its η-parts (Conjecture 5.3)
items.statement: For p odd and ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible: Char_{Λ_O}(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_f], ρ_f^*(1))/Im z_1(f)) = Char_{Λ_O}(H²_Iw(ℤ[1/p], ρ_f^*(1))), where H²_Iw(ℤ[1/p], ρ_f^*(1)) = Ker(H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_f], ρ_f^*(1)) → ⊕_{l∈Σ_{f,0}} H²_Iw(ℚ_l, ρ_f^*(1))) (printed with ℤ[1/p] as source, sourceIssues E9); decomposed into η-parts for characters η of Δ = Gal(ℚ(ζ_p)/ℚ).
items.note: Kato [28, Conj. 12.10]; ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L0 plans Kato's cohomological formulation.

items.name: Theorem 5.2: Kato's divisibility
items.statement: If ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible, p odd, and (a) some σ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})) has ρ_f/(σ − 1)ρ_f free of rank one over O, then Char_{Λ_O}(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_f], ρ_f^*(1))/Im z_1(f)) ⊂ Char_{Λ_O}(H²_Iw(ℤ[1/p], ρ_f^*(1))).
items.note: Kato [28, Thm. 12.4(4)] under a large-image hypothesis, relaxed to (a) by Skinner [50, after Thm. 2.5.4]; KatoEulerSystems L4.

items.name: μ- and λ-invariants of torsion Λ^η_O-modules (Corollary 5.4)
items.statement: Λ^η_O ≅ O[[T]]; f = ϖ^m g h with g distinguished of degree n and h a unit gives μ(f) = m, λ(f) = n, and μ(M), λ(M) via a generator of Char(M). Under (a), Conjecture 5.3 for f and η is equivalent to equality of the μ- and λ-invariants of the two sides (Corollary 5.4).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4 (Weierstrass theory, characteristic ideals, μ and λ).

items.name: Weierstrass preparation over complete local rings
items.statement: A power series over a complete local ring whose reduction is nonzero factors uniquely as a distinguished polynomial times a unit.
items.note: Used to define μ and λ.

items.name: Lemma 5.5: congruence modulo ϖ^m and residual isomorphism
items.statement: If ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible, f and g are congruent modulo ϖ^m (a_l ≡ b_l for almost all l) iff ρ_{f,m} ≅ ρ_{g,m}.
items.note: Pseudorepresentations (Nyssen [40]) and Chebotarev: GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1 and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.5.

items.name: Corollary 5.6: congruences of Kato's zeta morphisms
items.statement: Let f, g be normalized newforms with coefficients in E, ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible and the assumptions of §4 holding for ρ̄ = ρ̄_f. If f ≡ g (mod ϖ^m) then ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{f,l}(σ_l^{−1})·z_n(f) mod ϖ^m = ∏_{l∈Σ_0} P_{g,l}(σ_l^{−1})·z_n(g) mod ϖ^m as maps ρ^*_{f,m} → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_n, ζ_n], ρ^*_{f,m}(1)), Σ_0 = Σ_f ∪ Σ_g ∖ {p}.
items.note: Immediate from Theorem 4.3 at the two points x_f, x_g (the proof's 'ϖ^n' is ϖ^m, sourceIssues E11). Routed as a source of AutomorphicCongruences L4.

items.name: The residual zeta morphism z_{Σ,n}(ρ̄), the points X(ρ̄) and change of Σ
items.statement: Σ_ρ̄ = {p} ∪ ram(ρ̄); for Σ_ρ̄ ⊂ Σ ⊂ Σ′, ρ^m_{Σ′} ⊗ T_{ρ̄,Σ} ≅ ρ^m_Σ and z_{Σ′,n}(ρ^m_{Σ′}) ⊗ id = ∏_{l∈Σ′∖Σ} P_l(σ_l^{−1})·z_{Σ,n}(ρ^m_Σ) (79); z_{Σ,n}(ρ̄) is the base change to 𝔽 (a Λ_{n,𝔽}-linear map ρ̄^* ⊗_{𝔽[±1]} Λ_{n,𝔽} → H¹_Iw); X(ρ̄) = ∪_Σ Spec(T_{ρ̄,Σ})(ℤ̄_p) with its modular points X(ρ̄)^mod, and the specialisations z_{Σ,n}(ρ_x).
items.note: Routed as a source of AutomorphicCongruences L4.

items.name: Theorem 5.7 and Conjecture 5.8: residual non-vanishing and μ = 0
items.statement: For a character η of Δ, equivalent: (1) z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η ≠ 0; (2) μ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_f], ρ_f^*(1))^η/Im z_1(f)^η) = 0 for some x_f ∈ X(ρ̄)^mod; (3) the same for all x_f ∈ X(ρ̄)^mod. Conjecture 5.8: these always hold (motivated by Greenberg's μ = 0 conjecture for ordinary f).
items.note: Proof via (90)–(91) (mod ϖ sequences), freeness of H¹_Iw ([28, Thm. 12.4(3)]) and (88). Routed as a source of AutomorphicCongruences L4.

items.name: Theorem 5.9 and Conjecture 5.10: Kato's main conjecture for ρ̄
items.statement: Assume X(ρ̄)^mod_a ≠ ∅ (modular points with (a)) and Conjecture 5.8 for η. Then (1) H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η is free of rank one over Λ^η_𝔽; (2) H¹_Iw(…)^η/Im z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η and H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η are finite-dimensional. Conjecture 5.10 (the η-part of Kato's main conjecture for ρ̄): their 𝔽-dimensions are equal.
items.note: Uses Theorem 5.2 at x_f ∈ X^mod_a. Routed as a source of AutomorphicCongruences L4.

items.name: Theorem 5.11 and Conjectures 5.12–5.13: main conjectures for every point of the family
items.statement: Under the same assumptions, for any x ∈ X(ρ̄) (with Σ, O large): (1) H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η is free of rank one over Λ^η_O; (2) the quotient by Im z_{Σ,1}(ρ_x)^η and H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η are torsion; (3) both have μ = 0; (4) if x is modular or (b) some τ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})) has (ρ_x/(τ − 1)ρ_x)[1/p] one-dimensional, Char(H¹/Im z) ⊂ Char(H²). Conjecture 5.12 (η-part of Kato's main conjecture for ρ_x): equality of characteristic ideals, independent of Σ and equivalent to Conjecture 5.3 at x = x_f; Conjecture 5.13 (weak form): equality of λ-invariants.
items.note: Uses (80)–(89), the Euler–Poincaré formula and the general Euler system argument (EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.8) for (4). Routed as a source of AutomorphicCongruences L4.

items.name: Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15: constancy of the λ-defect
items.statement: Under the same assumptions, for every x ∈ X(ρ̄): λ(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η/Im z_{Σ,1}(ρ_x)^η) − λ(H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ], ρ_x^*(1))^η) = dim_𝔽(H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η/Im z_{Σ_ρ̄,1}(ρ̄)^η) − dim_𝔽 H²_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_ρ̄], ρ̄^*(1))^η, independent of x. Hence (Corollary 5.15) Conjecture 5.10 ⟺ the weak conjecture 5.13 for some x ⟺ for all x.
items.note: Proof via λ(M) = λ_𝔽(M/ϖ) − λ_𝔽(M[ϖ]) for μ(M) = 0 (92) and (91); the last display prints H¹ for H² (sourceIssues E12). Routed as a source of AutomorphicCongruences L4.

items.name: Theorem A.1: Kato's zeta morphism z^Ka_n(f)
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 prime to Σ_f there is a unique E-linear z^Ka_n(f) : V_1(f)_E → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_{f,n}, ζ_n], V_1(f)_E) such that for m ≥ 0 and γ ∈ V_1(f)_F the image ω_{γ,m} under exp^*_{m,1} lies in S_1(f)_F ⊗ ℚ(ζ_{np^m}) and u ⊗ x ↦ Σ_σ χ(σ)σ(x)per(u)^± sends ω_{γ,m} to L_{{p},n}(f^*, χ, k − 1)·γ^±; here V_1(f)_E is the maximal quotient of H¹(Y_1(N_f), 𝒱_{k/E}) on which T_l, S_l act by a_l, l^{k−2}ε_f(l) (Kato §§6.3, 8.3), S_1(f) the matching quotient of cusp forms and L_{Σ′,n}(f, χ, s) = Σ_{(m,Σ′n)=1} χ(m)a_m m^{−s}.
items.locator: Appendix A, Theorem A.1 and proof, pp. 265–267
items.note: Kato [28, Thm. 12.4, §§13.9–13.12] for n = 1 and its direct generalisation (μ_n(c, d, j) printed with d for d², sourceIssues E13); KatoEulerSystems L2–L3.

items.name: Remark A.2: integrality of Kato's zeta morphism
items.statement: If p is odd and ρ̄_f is absolutely irreducible, z^Ka_n(f) maps a G_ℚ-stable lattice V_1(f)_O into H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_{f,n}, ζ_n], V_1(f)_O) (Kato §13.12).
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L2 (integral version for the chosen lattice).

items.name: Lemma A.3, Definition A.4, Corollary A.5: the twisted zeta morphism z_n(f) and its characterisation
items.statement: V′_1(f)_A is the maximal quotient of H¹(Y_1(N_f), 𝒱^*_{k/A})(1) (printed Y(N_f), sourceIssues E14) on which T′_l, S′_l act by a_l, l^{k−2}ε_f(l); V′_1(f)_A ≅ V_1(f)_A^* and V′_1(f)_A(1 − k) ≅ V_1(f^*)_A (Lemma A.3). z_n(f) := twist^{⊗k} ∘ z^Ka_n(f^*) ∘ twist^{⊗(1−k)} (Definition A.4) is the unique E-linear V′_1(f)_E → H¹_Iw(ℤ[1/Σ_{f,n}, ζ_n], V′_1(f)_E(1)) whose dual-exponential images lie in S_1(f^*)_F ⊗ ℚ(ζ_{np^m}) with period L_{{p},n}(f, χ, k − 1)·((2πi)^{1−k}γ)^± (Corollary A.5); it is τ-equivariant and satisfies the Euler relations (Remark A.6).
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.3, Definition A.4, Corollary A.5, Remark A.6, pp. 268–269
items.note: Nakamura's normalisation of Kato's morphism, the form compared in Theorem 4.3. Routed as a source of KatoEulerSystems L2–L3.

items.name: Galois representations of newforms and their Hodge–Tate weights
items.statement: ρ_f : G_ℚ → GL_2(E) with tr ρ_f(Frob_l) = a_l, det = l^{k−1}ε_f(l) for l ∉ Σ_f (Shimura k = 2, Deligne k > 2); ρ_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights {−(k − 1), 0} (Scholl [48]); S_1(f)_E ≅ Fil^r D_dR(ρ_f) for 1 ≤ r ≤ k − 1; the decomposition (38) by local–global compatibility (Carayol, Deligne, Langlands, Saito, Scholl) and strong multiplicity one.

items.statement: For A ∈ Comp(O): V orthonormalizable if 𝔪-adically complete and separated with V/𝔪^iV free over A/𝔪^i; compact A-modules and ⊗̂; pro-free modules; V ↦ V^* = Hom_A(V, A) an anti-equivalence between orthonormalizable and pro-free modules ([15, Prop. B.11]); cofinitely generated X (ϖ-adically complete, O-torsion free, continuous action, (X/ϖ)[𝔪] finite) and X ↦ Hom_O(X, O) an anti-equivalence with O-torsion-free finitely generated modules ([15, Prop. C.5]); V ⊗̂_A X the ϖ-adic completion.

items.statement: V ⊗̂_A X is O-torsion free (B.5); V^* ⊗_A Hom_O(X, O) ≅ Hom_O(V ⊗̂_A X, O) (B.6); for X coadmissible, V ⊗̌_A X := lim_K V ⊗̂_A X^K and V^* ⊗_A X̃ ≅ (V ⊗̌_A X)~ as A[G]-modules (B.16).

items.statement: Colmez's exact functor MF from finite-length admissible smooth A[G_p]-modules to G_{ℚ_p}-representations (V(π) = MF(π)(ε)), extended to orthonormalizable admissible representations. routes.reason: L3 plans 'Nakamura's universal zeta morphism from the compatible modular/Hecke-level classes, including the completed-cohomology and local co-Whittaker input', and its specialisation to Kato's class: Theorems 1.1 and 4.3, Corollary 4.2, the construction of §4.1 and the steps of §§3.2–3.4 and 4.4 are planned there, and this paper is its source. L4 owns the pointwise consequences of the universal zeta element; the §5 application (congruences of zeta morphisms, the residual zeta morphism, Theorems 1.4, 5.7–5.14 and Conjectures 5.8–5.13) belongs inside it.

Siegel units, Beilinson elements, Kato's classes with their norm relations, the zeta value formula, Kato's zeta morphism and his divisibility are planned in L0–L4. The paper adds the full-level Iwasawa-theoretic packaging and normalisation that its comparison needs: the Hecke dictionary (Lemma 3.1), Fukaya–Kato's lemma on parabolic Iwasawa cohomology (Lemma 3.4), the characterisation Corollary 3.6, and the twisted morphism z_n(f) with its characterisation (Appendix A).

R31.4 plans Emerton's local–global compatibility from his unpublished manuscript, R31.3 the completed Hecke algebra and ρ^m, R31.6 Emerton's R = T theorems and R31.2 the classical specialisations. The paper's dual form for completed homology (Corollaries 2.5, 2.7, 2.8 and Lemma 2.6) is a supplier theorem of R31.4, not a construction for AutomorphicCongruences (whose L3 says missing supplier theorems go to their canonical roadmap).

CC.3 owns continuous duals and completed homology: the paper's completed Borel–Moore homology, its duality with compactly supported completed cohomology and the topological-module lemmas of Appendix B.1 belong there.

Colmez's functor (R30.3), the categories and projective envelopes (R30.2, R30.5) and Paškūnas' theorems (R30.5–R30.6) are planned. The consequences the paper draws — P̃ as the dual of the universal deformation of π̄ (Lemma B.23, Proposition B.26) and the removal of P̃ from Hom (Lemma B.27, Corollary B.28) — belong in R30.5 beside them.

SR.5 plans Whittaker functionals and co-Whittaker modules for GL_n in Helm's coefficient rings and names AutomorphicCongruences as their consumer; Lemma B.10 (endomorphisms of M ⊗ V) is a statement of that layer.
D7 is the sole owner of continuous cochains with compact coefficients and their derived base change; Lemmas B.29–B.31 and Corollary B.32 are such statements.

L0 owns parabolic and compactly supported cohomology of modular curves with boundary maps, Hecke actions and the Eichler–Shimura periods; the Hecke-equivariant Drinfeld–Manin splitting is its missing statement.
